page.overview:
Who is M142?

M142 was the tracking tag given to the Mosasaurus in .

M142 has more than 100 vertebrae for flexibility while swimming. Its mouth is long and has two rows of teeth on its upper jaw with a bite force of up to 16,000 pounds per square inch, enough to crush whale bones. Unlike the Nublar variant, its skin is relatively smooth, but its spine is lined with bumps along its length. The body surface is brown mixed with yellow-green and has black-brown patterns. The belly is white and has deep grooves along its length, similar to those found in baleen whales, helps the body resist water currents. Its tail is broad and paddle-shaped, with a triangular fin at the base that gives it immense power to propel its large body while swimming for 20 km/hr.

At one point around 2005, InGen built a research center on Ile Saint-Hubert. In 2010, an accident occurred and left the island deserted, and the experimental animals were released, including one Mosasaurus tagged "M142." The Mosasaurus had claimed the sea around the island as its territory for almost 20 years, despite the lack of a fence keeping it contained. In that time, it developed a symbiotic relationship with the Spinosaurus pack to enhance its hunting and territorial defense capabilities.

After living for 17 years, the Mosasaurus had grown to just over 30 meters in length. InGen still had its tracker with the tag ‘M142’ for a while before going bankrupt after Jurassic world went down. Big Pharma company Parker-Genix bought InGen's information and now tracks it. They plan to collect samples from it along with two other large animals on the island, Titanosaurus and Quetzalcoatlus. Company representative Martin hired Duncan's team and come to the island on the Essex.
